findings.title: Materials' 66-point lens gap signals collapse
findings.body: Materials trades at 15.69x forward but 33.75x trailing, a 66-point percentile gap between the two lenses. Analysts are underwriting 115 percent earnings growth, which would be a historic rebound from a depressed base — the market is pricing a recovery that has not yet appeared in reported results.

findings.title: Utilities' forward multiple defies trailing cheapness
findings.body: Utilities sits at the 10th percentile on forward P/E but the 1st percentile on trailing, yet the forward multiple is 16.07 versus 18.03 trailing. That means the market is paying a premium for expected stability even as reported earnings remain near their five-year low — a bet on resilience, not growth.

findings.title: Real Estate's forward premium ignores earnings decline
findings.body: Real Estate's forward P/E of 33.55 is its cheapest in five years at the 6th percentile, but the implied next-12m earnings growth is a 4 percent decline. The market is still assigning a rich multiple to a sector whose earnings are expected to shrink, suggesting the cheapness is relative to a falling base.
